findings.title: Conflicts with Al Noor GCC non-compete (in force until 14 Sep 2029): Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates
findings.explanation: Signed Al Noor MSA cl. 12.1 bars AtliQ and its Affiliates from analytics/AI/revenue-management work for any 'Hospitality Business' in the GCC, wherever the work is performed. Cl. 1.11 defines that as anyone who owns or operates hotels, resorts or serviced apartments, or who provides distribution, revenue-management or guest-analytics services to them (so hotel booking platforms count too). This draft covers that kind of work touching Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates. The Feb 2026 waiver covered the Seaside Hotels (Muscat) SOW only and does not help here. Evidence in this draft: 1.1 **TravelHub FZ-LLC**, a free zone limited liability company licensed by the Dubai Development Authority under licence no. 104772, with its office at Office 1408, Building 3, Dubai Internet City, P.O. Box 502211, Dubai, United Arab Emirates ("**TravelHub**" or "**Customer**"); and / (b) **Partner Hotel Ranking Module** — a ranking and recommendation service that scores, ranks and surfaces Partner Hotels in the United Arab Emirates and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to TravelHub users at the point of search and itinerary building, taking into account user fit, price competitiveness, partner commission tier, availability and conversion likelihood, and that drives the sort order of hotel results and "recommended stay" placements for booking through the TravelHub App; / 4.2 The initial launch markets for the Partner Hotel Ranking Module shall be Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh and Jeddah, with further cities in the UAE and KSA to be added by configuration.
findings.suggestion: Do not sign until one of: (a) a new written waiver from Al Noor under cl. 12.4 (as done for Seaside, Feb 2026); (b) GCC properties carved out of scope; or (c) counsel (Mehta Rao) confirms the restriction does not apply. Do not tell the client anything firm yet (counsel's advice, 25 Sep).
findings.quote: the Supplier undertakes that neither it nor any of its Affiliates shall, during the Restricted Period, directly or indirectly, provide data analytics, artificial intelligence or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC.
findings.precedent: 22 Sep queue meeting: nobody could find the Al Noor contract; Bhavin thought it had expired. It runs to 14 Sep 2029.

findings.title: Wrong AtliQ entity: AtliQ Inc (US) for a UAE counterparty
findings.explanation: Per atliq_entities.md, AtliQ Inc serves US clients only and Pvt Ltd serves everyone else. This draft names AtliQ Inc (US), so invoicing entity, tax regime (GST vs US) and bank account will not line up.
findings.suggestion: Replace with AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd (India) in the parties clause, signature block and notices.
findings.quote: 1.2 **AtliQ Inc**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal office at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, NJ 08540, USA ("**AtliQ**" or "**Developer**").
findings.precedent: Entity/invoice mismatches caused payment delays twice in 2025 (atliq_entities.md).

findings.title: Invoicing entity differs from the contracting entity
findings.explanation: The contract is signed by one AtliQ entity but invoices are raised by the other.
findings.suggestion: Make the contracting party and the invoicing party the same entity.
findings.quote: 7.1 Invoices under this Agreement shall be raised by AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd, GSTIN 27AAKCA4821F1Z3, on or after Acceptance of each milestone as set out in Schedule B.

findings.title: Foreign governing law: Emirate of Dubai and the applicable federal laws of the United Arab Emirates
findings.explanation: Governing law is Emirate of Dubai and the applicable federal laws of the United Arab Emirates. Karandeep's checklist: 'gov law → ours (India for Pvt Ltd, US for Inc)'. AtliQ has no presence there and would have to litigate abroad.
findings.suggestion: Ask for Indian law with Mumbai/Pune arbitration (Pvt Ltd) or a US state (Inc); fall back to a neutral seat such as SIAC/LCIA arbitration.
findings.quote: governed by the laws of Emirate of Dubai and the applicable federal laws of the United Arab Emirates
findings.precedent: Al Noor: DIFC law was accepted as the client's 'group standard'. Onshore Saudi/UAE law is a different, less predictable forum.

context_notes.body:
# Internal — contract queue (ad-hoc, 22 Sep)
Present: Karandeep, Bhavin, Dhaval, Jay

Called because three people chased Karandeep on the same morning.

Queue as of today (from Jay's list on the whiteboard):
- Harrington (Dhaval) — $210k, US, their paper — by **1 Oct**
- Lakeshore (Jay) — $64k, US — by **3 Oct**
- BlueOrchid pilot (Jay) — $38k — by **5 Oct**
- Gulf Crown (Bhavin) — $140k, Saudi — by **10 Oct**
- TravelHub (Karandeep) — $52k, Dubai — no date
- Rheinwerk (Bhavin) — €88k, Munich — draft arriving tomorrow, by **15 Oct**
- Sunrise SOW-2 (Dhaval) — $45k — Meera sending this week, wants by **8 Oct**

Discussion:
- Karandeep: reviewing late at night after calls, 10pm onwards. A client-paper MSA takes him 3–4 hrs properly. "Harrington alone is a whole evening and I haven't started."
- Dhaval raised ShopSwift — SOW sat 9 days in July waiting for review, Elena's budget slipped a quarter. "We lost that one to our own queue."
- Volume: Bhavin reckons last year was ~5 contracts/month, this year ~9 (MSAs, SOWs, NDAs, DPAs, amendments). Only Karandeep signs.
- Went through Gulf Crown headline terms. Midway Karandeep stopped: "didn't we sign something with the Dubai hotel people that stops us doing hotels in the Gulf?"
- Nobody could find the Al Noor contract quickly — Dhaval searched the shared drive, not there. Karandeep thinks it's in his email "somewhere".
- Bhavin: "I think that expired, no? It was a 2025 thing." Karandeep not sure.
- Jay: "is there a list of what we've agreed to not do?" — silence.
- Dhaval asked if we should send Harrington to counsel. Karandeep: "it's $210k, but Mehta Rao takes a week." Not decided.
- Bhavin: Gulf Crown can't slip, Faisal has a summit on the 14th.

Karandeep will go through them this weekend.

*(No owner, order of review, or deadline per contract was agreed. The Al Noor contract was not located during the meeting.)*
